met_criteria: AC1: DayTickRecord stores world_day/total_attempts/failure_count/degraded_count; DegradationTracker.history provides per-tick-type rolling record list
AC2: classify_outcome() returns exactly one OutcomeClass (acceptable/degraded/invalid) for every possible AppraisalAuditEntry state; it is a pure function testable in isolation
AC3: compute_rolling_rate() is implemented with configurable window_days (default 7) over range [current_day - window_days, current_day - 1]
AC4: is_auto_fallback_active() gates route() calls in simulate_day_bridged for T1, T2, and T4 when rate > threshold
AC5: AppraisalAuditLog extended with degradation_rates (dict[str, float]) and auto_fallback_active (dict[str, bool]) fields populated per-day
AC6: Forced-fallback outcomes are not recorded (design rule enforced in tick_bridge.py), allowing the window to slide naturally past bad entries; recovery tested explicitly
AC7: degradation_tracker is Optional[DegradationTracker] = None; all auto-fallback logic is guarded by tracker-not-None checks; backward compatibility test passes
AC8: 987 tests pass; no existing test files were modified

AC9: 32 new tests cover outcome classification (TestClassifyOutcome), rolling rate computation (TestRollingRate), threshold-triggered fallback (TestAutoFallbackThreshold), and window-based recovery (TestWindowBasedRecovery)
non_blocking_suggestions: The `_t4_auto_fallback = False` assignment inside the `else: _t4_target_rel is None` branch (tick_bridge.py ~line 1833) is redundant — the variable was already initialized to False at the top of the T4 block. Not a bug, just minor noise.

degradation_rates in the audit log is computed using `world_day + 1` as current_day (window includes today's records), while is_auto_fallback_active uses `world_day` (window excludes today). The difference is intentional and documented in a comment, but could cause confusion for callers who compare the rates in the audit log to the threshold — the stored rate may not directly correspond to the decision that was made for that day.

The tracker mutates in place (record_outcome modifies self.history). If callers share a tracker across concurrent simulations this would be unsafe, but given the current single-threaded simulation model this is not a real concern.
rationale: All 9 acceptance criteria are satisfied and all 6 review focus items check out. The three-class classification is exhaustive and mutually exclusive — every AppraisalAuditEntry state (llm_used=False → invalid; llm_used=True+failures → degraded; llm_used=True+clean → acceptable) maps to exactly one class. Rolling window boundary conditions are correctly handled: empty history returns 0.0, threshold check is strictly greater-than (not >=), and window arithmetic is consistent. Recovery is not just asserted but demonstrated by a full simulate_day_bridged call on day 15 after 7 bad records on days 1–7 (TestWindowBasedRecovery.test_recovery_reflected_in_audit_log). The tracker never touches state/growth/relationships/residuals — it only reads AppraisalAuditEntry results and writes to its own history dict. Backward compatibility is clean: the optional parameter with None default leaves the existing code path identical to pre-change behavior, confirmed by test_no_tracker_preserves_existing_behavior. The Pydantic BaseModel structure ensures JSON serializability, confirmed by serialization tests. No existing test files were modified. The full suite of 987 tests passes with no regressions.
